v01.title: Day 1
v01.author: R. Vance
v01.text: Relieved the summer crew at 14:10. Generator coughs when it's cold, breaker trips if you look at it. Hollis left the place tidy: mug on its hook, pencils sharpened. Dispatch says he walked out. Nobody walks anywhere out here. Logged the 20:00. The coffee tastes of diesel.

v02.title: Day 3
v02.author: R. Vance
v02.text: North mast reads 7 hPa under the south. The masts are 300 metres apart. That isn't weather, that's a fault. Sent it to Dispatch. Imogen said log it as read and don't recalibrate. Strange instruction from a weather service.

v03.title: Day 5
v03.author: R. Vance
v03.text: The fault only shows at night, and it moves. 4 hPa at 20:00. 11 at 02:00. Like something leaning on the north mast. Re-taped the window. The draught smells of salt, which makes no sense 200 km from open water.

v04.title: Day 6
v04.author: R. Vance
v04.text: Found Hollis's reading book under the bunk. Every page the same two columns, north and south. In the margin, every night at 03:00, a tally mark. Three strokes. Never four.

v05.title: Day 7
v05.author: R. Vance
v05.text: 03:00. Three knocks at the west door. I'm the only person for 400 km. I didn't open it. I'm writing this down so I remember that I didn't open it.

v06.title: Day 9
v06.author: R. Vance
v06.text: Tracks this morning, from the north mast straight to the west door. Boot prints, my size. I hadn't been out. The wind should have filled them by dawn. It hadn't.

v07.title: Day 10
v07.author: R. Vance
v07.text: Asked Imogen what happened to Hollis. She asked for the 22:00 reading. I asked again. She said the Service values continuity of the record. Then the line hissed and she was gone.

v08.title: Day 11
v08.author: R. Vance
v08.text: The drop has a rhythm. It deepens between 02:00 and 03:30 and lifts by dawn. Hollis's tallies sit on the same hours. He was logging the same thing. He just never wrote down what it was.

v09.title: Day 12
v09.author: R. Vance
v09.text: Moved my bunk into the generator room. It's louder and warmer and there's no window. You can't hear knocking over the generator. That's the point.

v10.title: Day 13
v10.author: R. Vance
v10.text: Four cans in the shed yesterday. Three this morning. I'm the only one here who drinks coffee, and the mug was on the table, not the hook. From now on I write down where I leave things.
